title: Incoterms rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ICC first published Incoterms in 1936; Incoterms 2020 in force since 1 January 2020; eleven three-letter trade terms setting out tasks, costs and risks in delivering goods from seller to buyer; Incoterms is an ICC trademark with a usage policy. No next edition mentioned; an ICC site search on 6 Nov 2026 found nothing on one.

title: Incoterms 2020
supports: Opened with WebFetch. DPU replaced DAT and the destination can be any place; under DPU the seller unloads, under DAP it does not; FCA allows an on-board bill of lading at the buyer's request; CIP requires higher insurance cover (Institute Cargo Clauses A) than CIF (Clauses C by default).

title: Know Your Incoterms
publisher: International Trade Administration, US Department of Commerce
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Seven Incoterms 2020 rules for any mode (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP) and four for sea and inland waterway (FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF); Incoterms do not set price, payment, transfer of title, customs documents, or liability for non-conforming goods and disputes.

title: Tips for New Importers and Exporters
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last modified 27 Aug 2024. The importer of record is responsible for correct entry documents and paying duties, even when a broker files; classify with the Harmonized Tariff Schedule; binding rulings can be requested under 19 CFR Part 177 and past rulings searched in CROSS; licensed brokers are not CBP staff.

title: E-Commerce Frequently Asked Questions
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last modified 2 Sep 2026. De minimis suspension covers goods valued at $800 or less by any mode, including mail; such shipments now need formal or informal entry; informal entry generally allowed up to $2,500; all duties, taxes and fees apply; gift and personal-article exemptions unchanged; new mail informal entry process.

title: E-Commerce
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last modified 4 Nov 2026. CBP moved the compliance date for new informal entry procedures for international mail from 22 Oct 2026 to 20 Jan 2027. Listed among the least sure facts: these dates have moved more than once.

title: Finding commodity codes for imports or exports
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last updated 22 Aug 2022. Commodity codes set duty and import VAT and show licences and preferences; only the first 6 digits are common worldwide; check codes supplied by overseas suppliers; use the online Trade Tariff (the tool itself blocked automated fetches).

title: Apply for an Advance Tariff Ruling
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last updated 2 Jun 2026. A legally binding HMRC decision on the commodity code for goods moving into or out of Great Britain, for the named holder only; apply before customs procedures are complete; replies in 30 to 120 days; Northern Ireland and EU trade use Binding Tariff Information instead.

title: Import goods into the UK: step by step
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no date shown. EORI number starting GB (or XI for Northern Ireland); choose a customs agent or do it yourself; find the commodity code; value the goods; check licences; make the declaration; reclaim import VAT with the C79; keep records.

title: VAT and overseas goods sold directly to customers in the UK
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last updated 13 May 2022. For consignments of 135 pounds or less sent from outside the UK, UK VAT is charged at the point of sale; the limit applies to the whole consignment, not each item; low value consignment relief (15 pounds or less) removed.

title: EU Customs Tariff (TARIC)
publisher: European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. TARIC is a multilingual database of EU tariff, trade and agricultural measures (third-country duties, preferences, quotas, anti-dumping, prohibitions and restrictions); it does not hold national VAT or excise rates; link to the TARIC consultation tool.

title: Tariff classification of goods
publisher: European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. The Combined Nomenclature is the EU's 8-digit coding built on the World Customs Organization's Harmonized System; the EBTI database holds all EU binding tariff information decisions.

title: EU Customs Reform
publisher: European Commission, Taxation and Customs Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 150 euro customs duty exemption ended on 1 Jul 2026; a temporary 3 euro customs duty per item on low-value consignments applies from 1 Jul 2026 to 1 Jul 2028 (8 Jun 2026 news); a 2 euro Union handling fee on small parcels from 1 Nov 2026 (7 Oct 2026 news; unit not stated); non-EU platforms and sellers handle customs formalities and duty; reform adopted 16 Sep 2026, in force 21 Sep 2026; Data Hub mandatory for e-commerce from 1 Jul 2028.

title: Domestic Claims
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Sender or recipient may claim on insured mail; damaged or missing contents: file at once and no later than 60 days after mailing; lost items: from 15 to 60 days (Priority Mail Express from 7 days); proof of insurance, value and damage photos; keep the packaging; decisions usually in 5 to 10 days; appeal within 30 days.

title: DMM 123 Priority Mail: Prices and Eligibility (dimensional weight)
publisher: United States Postal Service, Domestic Mail Manual
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Priority Mail parcels over 1 cubic foot (1,728 cubic inches) to zones 1 to 9 are priced on the greater of actual and dimensional weight; dimensions rounded up, volume divided by 139 and rounded up; 0.785 factor for non-rectangular parcels; capped at the 70-pound price. Revision marker 7-12-26 (likely 12 Jul 2026).

title: Holiday Shipping Dates
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 2026 recommended send-by dates for delivery by 25 Dec in the contiguous US: Ground Advantage 17 Dec, Priority Mail 18 Dec, Priority Mail Express 19 Dec.

title: Shipping Restricted, Hazardous and Perishable Mail
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no effective date shown. Publication 52 is the reference; small consumer lithium batteries mailable under conditions; damaged or defective devices with lithium batteries go by ground only and must be marked; prohibited items include air bags, ammunition, explosives and gasoline; penalties for mailing hazardous items.

title: 49 U.S. Code 14706: Liability of carriers under receipts and bills of lading
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (text of the US Code)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Subsection (e): a carrier may not allow less than 9 months to file a claim or less than 2 years to bring a civil action, the 2 years running from written notice that the claim is disallowed. Statute text; not a ruling on any case.

title: Business Guide to the FTC's Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule
supports: Opened with WebFetch; guide dated Sep 2011, edited Jan 2025. Sellers need a reasonable basis for shipping claims; 30 days when no time is stated (50 with a credit application); delay notices with a free way to cancel; refunds within 7 working days or one billing cycle; shipped means placed in the carrier's possession.

title: Shipping and delivery
supports: Opened with WebFetch; last checked by the EU 17 Aug 2026. Delivery within 30 days unless agreed otherwise; extra period then refund if still not delivered; the trader is responsible for damage from dispatch until the consumer receives the goods.

title: If something you ordered hasn't been delivered
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page last reviewed 22 Nov 2018, so listed among the least sure. Labelled a summary of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 (legislation.gov.uk returned empty pages to WebFetch): the seller is responsible for delivery even when it uses a courier, unless the buyer agreed another delivery place.

title: Online and distance selling for businesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no date shown. Deliver within 30 days unless agreed otherwise; customers may cancel up to 14 days after delivery; up to 12 months more if not told about the right.

title: Drivers' hours: GB domestic rules
supports: Opened with WebFetch; no date shown. Goods vehicle drivers under GB domestic rules: no more than 10 hours driving on public roads a day, 11 hours duty a day; hours recorded on a weekly record sheet or tachograph; some exemptions.

title: Driving time and rest periods
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Regulation 561/2006: daily driving up to 9 hours (10 hours twice a week), 56 hours a week, 90 hours over two weeks; a 45-minute break after 4.5 hours, which can be split 15 plus 30; 11 hours daily rest.

title: Vehicle Routing Problem
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. The vehicle routing problem finds routes for several vehicles; with one vehicle it is the travelling salesperson problem; variants with vehicle capacity and time windows; minimising the longest route rather than total distance when all drops should finish early.

title: The Bullwhip Effect in Supply Chains
supports: Opened with WebFetch (public excerpt only). Hau L. Lee, V. Padmanabhan and Seungjin Whang, Spring 1997: order swings grow larger the further they move up the supply chain, shown by Procter and Gamble's Pampers orders.

title: Warehouse Science
publisher: John J. Bartholdi III, Georgia Institute of Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free textbook and tools on managing time and space in a warehouse: slotting fast movers in forward pick areas, order picking methods, pick paths and product affinity from sales history.

title: Shippo MCP Server
supports: Opened with WebFetch; undated. Hosted MCP server at mcp.shippo.com; users sign in with their Shippo account; compares rates, buys labels, tracks parcels, validates addresses, builds customs declarations and runs batches. The page also held instructions addressed to AI agents, which were not followed.

title: Logisticians: Occupational Outlook Handbook
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Median pay 82,320 dollars a year (May 2025); employment projected to grow 18 percent from 2025 to 2035; about 26,600 openings a year.

title: 2025 Retail Returns Landscape
publisher: National Retail Federation with Happy Returns (a UPS company)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; published 15 Oct 2025. Projected 849.9 billion dollars of US retail returns in 2025; an estimated 19.3 percent of online sales returned; 9 percent of returns judged fraudulent. Industry survey; sample size not shown on the page.
